test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 29 Jan 2021 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Which option correctly describes the taungya system?

options.text: It is the management and protection of forests and achieving afforestation on barren lands
It is the system of growing trees or shrubs around or among crops or pastureland
It is the system of growing agricultural crops between rows of planted trees
It is setting up a fire to a piece of land to increase fertility of soil

solution:
The correct answer is __**It is the system of growing agricultural crops between rows of planted trees.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **The taungya **is a **system **whereby **villagers **and **sometimes forest plantation workers **are given the **right to cultivate agricultural crops **during the **early stages **of **forest plantation establishment**.
 
• **Cultivation **is **often allowed **to **continue until trees shade crops **due to **canopy closure**.
 
• **The taungya **is a **Burmese word coined **in **Burma in 1850s**. The **taungya system **was **introduced **into **India by Brandis **in **1890 **and the **first taungya plantations **were raised in **1896 in North Bengal**.
 
• **Types of Taungya**:
 
 
• **Departmental Taungya**: Under this, agricultural crops and plantations are raised by the forest department.
 
• **Leased Taungya**: The forest land is given on lease to the person who affects the highest money for raising Agril.
 
• **Village Taungya**: This is the most successful of all the three Taungya systems.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Afforestation **is the **planting **or** adding **of **trees **in an **area **where there **was never a forest or plantation**. This is **a method **to **create a new forest**.
 
• **Agroforestry **is a **collective name **for **land-use systems **and **technologies **where woody **perennials **(trees, shrubs, palms, bamboos, etc.) are **deliberately used **on the same **land-management **units as **agricultural crops **and/or animals, in some form of **spatial arrangement **or **temporal sequence**.
 
• **Soil fertility **can be further **improved by incorporating cover crops **that **add organic matter **to the soil, which leads to improved soil structure and promotes healthy, fertile soil.
